text:
maria: Early brain dump — proposal to add a lightweight 'budget-shadow' layer in front of admission to unify tenant budgets + model-level quotas. Goal: single place to evaluate fairness, per-tenant burst windows, and a cheap fast-pass check for edge proxies. Thinking: keep in-memory fast-path, async durable backing, and clear fallback to current token-based admission if anything goes wrong. Thoughts?
kevin: +1 for a fast-path. question: where does ownership live? admission-service or token-broker?
zach: curious about telemetry costs — duplicating checks could double the read QPS. we need a sketch of read/write patterns. can you add estimated RPS?
maria: rough numbers: peak requests 20k/s across frontdoors, ~150k checks/s at micro-op level after batching. fast-path should be <=1 allocation read (in-memory) per request; durable write only on state change (leases / bursts).
olivia: compatibility note: private deployments often run with local proxies and high egress constraints. the fast-path must be self-contained without a central call for strict VPC installs. prefer local in-memory with passive gossip for global caps.
sara: security flags — abuse detection relies on heuristics that need token-level data. if we shadow budgets, make sure we preserve signal fidelity for detection and for forensic logs. also: ensure KMS keys not exposed in proxies.
raj: migration plan idea: start with read-only shadow where budgets computed by new layer but admission still uses old path. We'll run a 2-week comparison window, collect divergence metrics, then flip progressive canary. DB change: new table budget_shadow{tenant_id, model_key, window_start, used, version}. needs 1 write/op on burst lease, optimistic concurrency. thoughts on TTLs?
olivia: prefer 1s sliding windows for fast fairness, with 5s aggregation in telemetry. too many small windows blow up storage.
kevin: concerning eventual consistency: if shadow diverges you want deterministic fallback. propose: check = fast-path(in-memory) -> if miss then call canonical admission -> record in shadow async -> return canonical result. only flip enforcement when divergence < 0.5% for 24h.
maria: API sketch for the fast-path (very small):
```
POST /v1/budget_shadow/check
{ "tenant": "t123", "model": "llama-2-7b", "tokens": 120 }
Response 200/429 { "allowed": true, "remaining": 10240, "version": "v42" }
```
We should keep it opaque: admit vs probe modes.
zach: telemetry: add a tag `shadow_mode:{probe|enforce|fallback}` and emit dimensioned counters for `check_latency_ms` and `decision_source`. Also track `stale_version` counter when in-memory version < backing version.
sara: on abuse side: when in enforce, make sure we still forward events to abuse-detector with raw token context (sampled) and decision provenance. Also add a kill-switch in the control plane to revert enforcement per region.
raj: ops runbook bullets: 1) start probe in a single prod region for 48h; 2) compare false-positive / false-negative rates vs current admission; 3) run 5% traffic enforce; 4) increase if SLOs stable. add a job to reconcile shadow table every minute.
kevin: implementation tradeoffs: option A keep shadow state in Redis cluster (fast, simpler) vs B use local memory with periodic sync (faster reads, more complex). My vote: Redis for initial rollout, local memory + gossip in later opt.
maria: +1 Redis first. Raj, can you mock the schema and estimated memory?
raj: estimated keys: ~500k active tenant-model combos, each key ~64 bytes -> ~32MB base, with modest over-provisioning 256MB. Redis cluster fine. Reconcile job will expire keys with no updates for 2m.
olivia: one more: edge proxies need a small lib to call check or do local fast-pass. keep client API tiny (see sketch).
kevin: rollback plan: if canary shows >1% degradation in p95 latency or >0.2% increase in false rejections, flip enforcement off and collect traces.
maria: ok next steps: 1) create a spec PR with schema + API + telemetry; 2) implement Redis-backed probe mode; 3) run 48h probe in region eu-west-1; 4) iterate. assigning owners: @kevin infra for redis + client libs, @raj db + reconcile jobs, @zach telemetry + dashboards, @sara security review.
sara: noted, will schedule quick threat model review. also propose retention rules for shadow logs (90d) and an audit export for enterprise customers.
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: infra/redis-proxy v0.21 -> eu-west-1 at 2025-12-03T09:00Z (canary 5% traffic).
maria: thanks all — will open the PR and link to this thread. please react with :thumbsup: if you can pick up the assigned item.
